blocks.text: **“A woman has cord prolapse. What do you do?”**

“I recognize this as an obstetric emergency. I would immediately call for senior obstetric, anaesthetic and neonatal assistance and ask someone to document the time. I would perform a vaginal examination and manually elevate the presenting part to relieve cord compression. I would place the woman in an appropriate position such as knee-chest or a steep lateral/head-down position, stop oxytocin if it is running and avoid unnecessary manipulation of the cord.

I would continuously assess the fetal heart rate but would not delay delivery for investigations. I would determine whether vaginal delivery is immediately achievable. If the cervix is fully dilated and the head is low, an appropriately qualified operator may perform an expedited operative vaginal delivery. If vaginal birth is not imminent, I would proceed urgently to Caesarean delivery while maintaining measures to relieve cord compression.
After delivery I would ensure neonatal resuscitation and assessment, particularly for hypoxic injury, and document the event comprehensively.”

**“Cord prolapse: call for help, elevate the presenting part, position mother, stop oxytocin, don't manipulate the cord, and deliver immediately — vaginally if birth is truly imminent, otherwise emergency Caesarean.”**
